title: Throughput resonance scratch notebook (resonance tests)
content:
Goal:
Quick investigation into intermittent throughput drops + tail latency spikes that look like a resonance effect when batch windows align with ingress periodicity. Running lightweight replay and synthetic drivers to reproduce. Notes to self + raw logs below.

Setup:
- Model: llama2-13b-quant (int8 fastpath variant)
- Runtime build: local dev image rwinf/runtime:dev-20240910
- Hardware: 1x A10G (cloud dev node), 32GB RAM, kernel preemptions observed earlier
- Serving config: max_batch: 16, batch_timeout_ms: 8, continuous_batching: enabled
- Traffic driver: synthetic Poisson + periodic pulse generator (python small script)
- Warm cache vs cold cache toggles tested

Commands run (approx):
- run driver: python bench/driver.py --pattern pulse --qps 220 --pulse-mag 120 --pulse-interval 3s --seed 42 --concurrency 40
- tailer: go run tools/trace-collector --stream pprof,events --out tmp/resonance-20240912.trace

Observations (raw):
- At steady qps=220 baseline (no pulses) p50 ~ 23ms, p95 ~ 86ms, p99 ~ 280ms, overall throughput ~ 210 qps (some backpressure).
- Introduce pulse pattern (3s interval, +120 qps for 200ms) -> within 2 pulses see throughput oscillation: node overshoots then underutilizes.
- Cold cache start: first 30s p99 spikes to 1.6s (expected). After warmup, recurring p99 spikes at pulse boundaries: 0.7-0.9s for 2-3 intervals only.

Representative latency timeline (ms) for a 20s window (sample):
  time 0s:  24, 28, 23, 25, 22, 26, 27
  time 3s:  30, 300, 320, 28, 26, 24   <-- big synchronous tail cluster (pulse boundary)
  time 6s:  25, 27, 24, 600, 26       <-- single straggler from multiplexed batch
  time 9s:  26, 30, 33, 29, 28
  time12s:  28, 270, 290, 32          <-- repeated pattern

Quick hypothesis:
- "Resonance" arises when the pulse alignment causes many requests to enter the batch window right before deadline, producing a large batch that increases per-token compute time and KV cache pressure, then the next window sees underutilization while kernel warmup/garbage cycles happen.
- We see two failure modes: (A) batched stragglers inside giant batches causing tail spikes; (B) downstream work-stealing/eviction (GPU memory reclaim / cuda context thrash) causes a multi-request pause ~200-900ms.

Micro-experiments and results:
1) Reduce batch_timeout_ms from 8ms -> 3ms (keep max_batch 16):
   - p95 improved slightly from 86ms -> 72ms, p99 reduced from 280ms -> 190ms under pulse; throughput reduced ~5% but smoother.
2) Set max_batch=8, timeout=8ms:
   - p99 under pulse down to ~150-220ms; throughput down ~12%.
3) Disable continuous_batching (force single-request fast path when available):
   - p50 similar, p95 improved in pulse windows, p99 rare but still occasional large spikes (GPU eviction traces co-occur).
4) Add jitter to driver pulse interval (random +/- 200ms):
   - resonance effect dampened; p99 spikes become less synchronized and magnitudes drop by ~40%.

Raw perf counters (sample from metrics exporter at spike):
- GPU util: 92% -> dips to 18% during drop windows; 1-2s later recovers.
- GPU mem alloc/free events: bursts at pulse boundary (observed via nvprof logs).
- Kernel queue length: jumps from 3 -> 18 for 120ms windows.

Notes to self (actionable):
- Try a hybrid approach: smaller max_batch (8) + small timeout (4ms) + request spacing jitter at ingress. Expect smoother SLOs with small throughput hit.
- Investigate CUDA memory allocator fragmentation patterns; reproducible in dev node. Try setting allocator flags (TF_CUDA_ALLOCATOR_ON) or use jemalloc tuning.
- Add a lightweight local health check to detect immediate batch-size surge and momentarily divert to a cheaper variant (e.g., 7b) as graceful degradation path.
- Instrument per-request kernel latency and GPU mem ops in finer granularity for next run.

Open questions:
- Is the big contributor the batch-induced compute time (long single-batch kernels) or allocator churn? (nvprof suggests both). Need isolated runs where we pin batch size and measure just kernel durations.
- How does quantization variant impact peak kernel latency? The int8 path may have different cache behavior. Run same test with float16 13b.
- Can we reproduce on Dedicated pool (multi-GPU) to confirm cluster-level routing interactions?

Next runs (planned):
- 2024-09-14: pin batch sizes in driver (simulate exact batches of 4,8,12,16 arriving) and capture GPU kernel durations (nvprof) + allocator stats.
- 2024-09-16: repeat with model float16 and int8 on same node.
- 2024-09-18: run with Dedicated small instance (2xA10G) to see cross-device interaction.

Quick summary (for Slack share):
- Observed synchronized tail spikes when ingress pulses align with batch windows -> calling this "throughput resonance".
- Short-term mitigation: reduce max_batch and/or reduce batch timeout, add ingress jitter.
- Medium-term: investigate allocator fragmentation + consider fast fallbacks to smaller model variant.

TODO (short):
- [ ] Run pinned batch kernel-only experiments (no allocator churn).
- [ ] Add exporter metrics for per-batch kernel duration + mem alloc counts.
- [ ] Check GH PR for allocator experiment (linked).

Random notes / half-baked thoughts:
- Could use a tiny client-side rate-smoothing shim that micro-jitters arrival times to avoid alignment. Might be a cheap, customer-friendly fix.
- If resonance persists across multiple nodes in Dedicated, might be a scheduling artifact (VM vCPU steal). Add host-level perf counters in next run.

End of scratchpad.

-- Ori
